reason: The workspace root holds only build configuration (package scripts, six tsconfig files, eight vitest configurations, the tsdown configuration, a Makefile); in Go that job is done by go.mod and go.work, go test lanes and one small sequential gate runner.

The gate scheduler, 51 verify scripts, 17 generators and the release scripts become Go tests, go/analysis checkers, one registry-driven catalog generator and GoReleaser; gates that guard npm publication, bilingual documents and contributor process are not carried over.

The 35 workflows are replaced by harness jobs added to this repository's ci.yml and release.yml plus one credentialed scenario workflow; weighted approval, issue lifecycle and stale-pull-request automation are dropped as repository governance, not product.
The recorded-session replay system is kept, but the 2,039 fixture files are in upstream's session format and are not reused; the Go corpus is recorded from the Go product in its own format.

Budgeted user-path performance gates are kept as Go tests that run the built binary in a fresh child with synthetic inputs and constants held in source; the eight upstream benchmark directories name the paths to measure.

The owner keeps the documentation website: the VitePress projection of docs/ is replaced by a static site that Hugo, a Go generator pinned as a docs-only tool in its own module and workflow, builds from the same Markdown without copying it; the second locale and the theme extensions (viewer, table filter, code groups, Markdown twins, search) are not carried over in the first version.

The 22 skills are working instructions for contributors to the upstream repository, not part of the product; the test-isolation rules worth keeping are restated in the test decisions and the rest is not copied.
The JavaScript test runner behind every upstream lane is replaced by go test and the standard testing package.
Mock functions used by the remote-service test double are replaced by hand-written fakes that implement Go interfaces; no mocking library is needed.
V8 coverage instrumentation is replaced by the Go toolchain's compiled-in coverage, which also covers child processes.
It is the base class of a custom reporter that prints uncovered locations; go tool cover reports uncovered lines from the profile.
Property-based tests in five upstream suites are replaced by native fuzz targets with committed seed and crasher inputs.
The simulated browser document for client component tests is replaced by rendering the Go handler and parsing its HTML, because the UI is rendered by the host.
Role and text queries over a simulated document are replaced by small query helpers over the parsed HTML tree.
It mounts React components in tests; the Go UI has no React components, so component tests render Go templates and assert on the HTML.
The per-package JavaScript bundler is replaced by go build, which links one binary from the module.
The front-end bundler and development server (three major versions installed at once) is replaced by static assets embedded in the binary with the embed package.
It maps TypeScript workspace imports to source files for the JavaScript test runner; Go resolves imports from the module graph, so the problem does not exist.
It hashes CSS-module class names and rewrites url() references inside bundled JavaScript client packages; the Go UI serves plain embedded stylesheets and has no client bundles.
The TypeScript runner used for every repository script and for launching the CLI from source is replaced by go run and go generate.
The JavaScript linter is replaced by gofmt, go vet and staticcheck.
The type-aware rule backend for the JavaScript linter is replaced by go vet and staticcheck, which always analyse type-checked code.
Formatting rules are replaced by gofmt, which fixes layout instead of reporting it.
Duplicate-branch and identical-expression rules are replaced by staticcheck checks of the same kind.
Cross-file clone detection is not carried over; the static-check decision records that it is left out and can be added later as one more tool.
The npm package manager is replaced by Go modules with go.sum verification and a go.work workspace.
It supplies a second JavaScript package manager for a generated-project test; a Go product has no npm package managers to be compatible with.
It lints the entry points of published npm packages; the Go product publishes a binary and a module tag, not npm packages.
It reads pyproject.toml files inside the third-party notices generator; the Go notice is generated from the module graph by go-licenses.
It parses licence expressions inside the third-party notices generator; go-licenses classifies module licences instead.
The git hook manager is replaced by one checked-in pre-commit script enabled through git's core.hooksPath setting; CI remains the authority.

It is the static site generator that publishes docs/ as a website; the owner keeps the website, and the Go design generates it from the same Markdown with Hugo, a generator written in Go that is pinned as a docs-only tool and never linked into dsh.

It renders Mermaid diagrams inside the documentation website; in the Go site one code-block template turns a mermaid fence into an element that the vendored Mermaid script draws in the reader's browser.
It is the component framework of the documentation website theme; the Go site's layouts are Go templates in the generator's own template language, so no component framework is needed.

The file records 1,204 existing type assertions to unknown in 477 files that the no-new-unknown-casts gate tolerates; in Go the analogous checker (unchecked type assertions and unsafe) is required from the first commit with inline reasoned exceptions, so no baseline is created.

The file records 42 existing reads of the cordis root context in 27 files; the Go port has one accessor, Context.Root, and a checker restricts its callers before any harness code calls it, so there is nothing to record.
The baseline for the empty-catch rule is already empty upstream; the Go analogue, a discarded error value, is rejected by a checker from the first commit unless the site carries a reason.

The file lists nine heavy suites that run without instrumentation so the per-file 100% gate stays affordable; Go coverage is compiled in, cheap and covers child processes, and the Go rule is one uniform package floor with no list of exempt suites or files.

The event graph under-reports Client listeners because one TypeScript program cannot hold both the Host and Client context declarations; the Go design has one program and generates catalogs from the running registries, so the split does not exist.
A transitive dependency is forced to one version with no stated reason; the Go module policy requires a reason comment on every replace, exclude, version floor and tool pin, checked by a test.
It is an entry in pnpm's allow-list of dependencies permitted to run npm install scripts; downloading a Go module never runs code, so there is no install-script allow-list.
It is a denial in pnpm's npm install-script allow-list for an optional native addon; Go modules have no lifecycle scripts, so the mechanism does not exist.
It exempts the pinned pnpm package manager from pnpm's own release-age rule; in Go the toolchain version is selected by go.mod and verified by the checksum database, with no exemption list.
